A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TerraMind and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and supplementary material. Content can be matched reliably across the reorganization and expanded evaluation.

before.justification: v1 reports original pretraining, tokenizer reconstruction, generation, zero-shot, few-shot, PANGAEA, and TiM results, including supplementary experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds quantitative generation evaluations, tokenizer training curves, and additional qualitative analyses.

M1.justification: The core dual-scale architecture, tokenization approach, loss, and TiM mechanism remain. v2 Section 11.1 adds a large-scene inference adaptation using overlapping 224-by-224 generations and averaging their overlaps. The new TiM subsection mainly elaborates the previously introduced technique.

E1.justification: TerraMesh, the nine PANGAEA tasks, EuroSAT, METER-ML, and South Africa crop mapping are retained. v2 adds large-area generation scenarios in Singapore and Santiago de Compostela, including cloud-obscured inputs, and extends contextual geolocation sampling from bare land to urban areas.

E2.justification: The tokenizer reconstruction comparison between v1-B and v1-B-single in v1 Table 9 disappears from v2 Table 10. The U-Net, ViT, and single-scale PANGAEA comparisons in v2 Table 6 already appeared in v1 Table 11. MetaEarth is added only to the descriptive architecture comparison, without evaluated performance.

E3.justification: v2 introduces quantitative generation evaluation using MAE, RMSE, SSIM, and PSNR with 10 diffusion steps, separately examining pixel and token inputs in Tables 3 and 14. Tokenizer evaluation changes from polarization-specific MSE reporting to modality-level MAE/RMSE reporting. These substantially revise the generative evaluation, while the downstream benchmark protocols remain stable.

E4.justification: v2 adds a controlled comparison of generation from pixel versus token inputs, FSQ-versus-VQ reconstruction-loss and gradient-norm curves, urban geolocation error analysis, and large-scene case studies. It removes the tokenizer intensity and inter-metric correlation analyses. The original optical geolocation example is retained as Figure 15, rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: v1 reports estimated correlations between reconstructed and true SAR intensities and between reconstruction metrics; v2 removes this statistical analysis. Few-shot results still report averages over 200 runs, with no new confidence intervals, seed disclosures, or significance tests.

E6.justification: v2 adds generation results in Tables 3 and 14 and replaces the tokenizer reconstruction results with differently structured measurements, which do not establish a same-setting performance decline. CLIP few-shot scores change, including EuroSAT 1-shot 5-way accuracy from 52.39 to 57.00. The complete PANGAEA results and reported water/crop TiM scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: v2 Section 4.4 adds mathematical definitions of TiM's generated-input augmentation and recursive prediction, including Equations 5–6. The existing Dirichlet sampling, cross-entropy, random-loss calculation, and chained-generation equations are retained; no new theorem or proof is supplied.

C1.justification: v2's introduction adds the claim that TerraMind uniquely demonstrates benefits of autoregressive modeling for EO relative to MAE, contrastive, and diffusion approaches. The central claims about dual-scale learning, any-to-any generation, TiM, and downstream superiority remain substantively unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 replaces the earlier interpretation of very high SAR reconstruction quality with an account acknowledging structural deviations. It adds interpretations concerning optical/radar generation asymmetry, elevation errors, semantic compression tradeoffs, urban/bare-land confusion, and TiM's benefit from a trainable encoder. These materially revise the discussion of generative capabilities and limitations.

D1.justification: v2 Section 8.1 substantially expands tokenizer documentation, including decoder architecture, patch sizes, quantizer configuration, diffusion schedule, optimizer, precision, and regularization. The abstract changes resource release from planned to completed. However, the added claims of EMA use conflict with Section 9's retained statement that EMA was omitted, limiting reproducibility.

R1.justification: v2 adds MetaEarth and contrasts its optical generation with TerraMind's any-to-any capability. It adds an AnySat reference for a model already discussed in v1, mentions ViT-VQGAN influences, and introduces autoregressive positioning. The JUWELS reference disappears with the acknowledgements; most related work remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Localized rewrites expand tokenizer and dual-scale explanations and add a dedicated TiM subsection. Generation and geolocation passages move into reorganized supplementary sections, and the acknowledgements are removed. Most of the introduction, benchmark narrative, and conclusion remain closely matched.

P2.justification: v2 adds generation tables, FSQ/VQ plots, an urban geolocation map, and extensive large-area imagery. It restructures the tokenizer table and revises radar visualizations. Figure 1 moves before the abstract, the complete PANGAEA table moves into the main text, and existing geolocation/generation figures are redistributed.

improvement.justification: v1 supports generation mainly through selected qualitative examples; v2's generation tables and FSQ/VQ curves provide useful quantitative scrutiny and clearer discussion of failure modes. These gains modestly strengthen the paper. They are limited by contradictory EMA documentation, the stale tokenizer-table caption, and the claim of only minor compression effects despite optical-to-DEM SSIM changing from 0.942 with pixel inputs to 0.5728 with token inputs.
